correctness.rationale: For every prime power q>2, edge products of an even vertex cycle have a Q-to-one image equal to the parity-product toric hypersurface; monomials are evaluation independent. An r-dimensional coefficient subspace has a d-dimensional annihilator plane, with at most Q^d nonzero-coordinate points by injective coordinate projection. Balanced odd/even edge grouping attains this for every 1<=d<=k. Equality forces all coordinate functionals to be nonvanishing one-variable linear forms using F_q^*+F_q^*=F_q; the hypersurface identity forces each group imbalance divisible by Q and the scalar product constraint. The group-rescaling action yields Q^(2k-d-1) distinct planes per admissible unlabeled partition. This proves both weights and counts, including q=3 modular cases, with no dependence on finite exhaustive experiments. Independent finite RREF and image enumeration in verify.py returns VERIFY_OK; its restrictions are explicitly delimited.

originality.rationale: The original cycle paper arXiv:2608.30407v1 §4.2 covers the ordinary weight enumerator/minimum distance, not simultaneous zeros of r independent codewords or the complete minimizing-subcode population. Related higher-weight results concern the larger full square-free hypersimplex space (arXiv:2002.10920v4) or projectively parameterized complete-bipartite codes (arXiv:1611.06405v2), not this sparse affine cycle-edge family for 2k>=6. The initial edge-code paper arXiv:2404.02301v1 provides definitions and minimum distances. value.rationale: The generalized Hamming-weight sequence governs minimum supports of all r-subcodes and is not encoded by the ordinary Hamming weight distribution. The theorem determines every high-r weight of an infinite graph-code family, the full population and geometry of minimum-support subcodes for every q>2, and the exact small-field modular effect / large-field balanced-partition transition. A sharp boundary at r=k explains saturation of the linear-section projection bound. These are structural and operationally relevant invariants, not a fixed tiny computation or generic parameter substitution.
